item.content:encoded:
Misiorowski will start Game 1 of the NLCS against the Dodgers on Sunday.
Misiorowski took the mound to begin the opening contest of the NLDS against San Diego, and the Brewers will turn to their ace again to begin their best-of-seven series against Los Angeles. The 24-year-old is a strong contender to take home the NL Cy Young Award after posting a 1.80 ERA and 0.80 WHIP across 174.2 innings in the regular season, but he wasn't quite as dominant during his first postseason outing, allowing two runs on four hits and a walk while fanning six batters in four innings.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Déjà vu all over again in Dodgers vs. Brewers NLCS rematch
item.dc:creator: Estevão Maximo

item.content:encoded:
Baseball postseason, for all of its unpredictability, has brought us the meeting of the two best teams in the sport to determine the National League representative in the World Series. Ahead of last season's NLCS, the angle of David versus Goliath was heavily played in virtually any analysis—it didn't help the more centered angle that the Dodgers steamrolled the Brewers on their way to a sweep. This time around it might not be that simple.
The similarities are evident, with the Brewers, yet again, having home-field advantage as a team that better maximized its skill set in the regular season, all while the Dodgers remain the favorites to advance, as was the case last season. Having said that, foolish are those who project a similar imbalance to that of the previous NLCS—the expectation of a more tightly contested series goes through pitching.
It may appear like a small factor, but the fact that both teams won their Division Series in four games means that Pat Murphy and Dave Roberts can line up their pitching in the ideal way for this Championship Series. And pitching is the great equalizer here, as both teams are stacked in that department and neither offense is currently hot enough to the point of putting into question the likelihood of a series dominated by elite pitching.
For all the talent on the mound for the Dodgers, the odds-on favorite to win the NL Cy Young pitches on the other side in Jacob Misiorowski. He is joined by the rookie Logan Henderson at the front end of a pitching staff tied with the Dodgers for the second-highest ERA+ in baseball. Last year's Brewers ace, Freddy Peralta, was good, not great, in the series against Los Angeles, and that applied to several key Brewers pitchers in order for the Dodgers to sweep the series in four without major offensive explosions.
With starting pitching on both sides able to dominate, the Dodgers have an advantage from last season's team in that the bullpen brings a much greater sense of reliability, not only in depth but also in the backend. We probably get the sense most fans will watch Edwin Díaz and Tanner Scott, waiting for them to fail all the way until the hypothetical final out of the World Series—but they've done enough to earn Dave Roberts' trust, and the plethora of options behind them ready for a high-leverage spot if things go south isn't to be ignored.
Such emphasis on pitching is a must from the Brewers side because offensively, despite Jake Bauers' breakout campaign at first, the Dodgers still retain a heavy advantage, one that might even be currently underplayed ahead of the series. With little to no action from some of its top hitters, the Dodgers weren't brilliant, but they still got theirs in key spots against the feisty Braves. Last postseason, the Dodgers offense wasn't bombastic against Milwaukee, but it did enough to capitalize on strong pitching, while the Brewers' attack was nowhere to be found against elite Dodger starting pitching.
Second to last in regular-season homers and top five in stolen bases, the Brewers' offense's best course of action to put a dent in Dodger pitching is through generating action on the basepaths — putting the bat on the ball and pressuring a defense that has vulnerabilities (I won't name any names — Teoscar Hernández, cough, cough). It's nearly unfathomable to imagine Blake Snell or Tyler Glasnow escaping a five-walk outing with just one run against the Brewers like they did facing the Braves.
All season long, the National League has clearly proven to be the superior league. It's only fitting that the winner of the NLCS, whoever that is, will enter the Fall Classic as the favorite to win it all — the Dodgers in pursuit of a threepeat and the Brewers in search of their first title.

item.content:encoded:
Dodgers make Tarik Skubal decision that should worry Brewers before NLCS showdown originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
The Los Angeles Dodgers are four victories away from returning to the World Series, and manager Dave Roberts has revealed how his team plans to attack the Milwaukee Brewers in the National League Championship Series.
Roberts announced Friday that Tarik Skubal will start Game 1 on Sunday, with Yoshinobu Yamamoto scheduled to pitch Game 2 on Monday. The decision gives Los Angeles two of baseball's most accomplished pitchers to begin a series that features the National League's top two regular-season teams.
The announcement also provides another reminder of the extraordinary pitching depth the Dodgers have assembled. Los Angeles is attempting to win its third consecutive World Series championship, and its starting rotation could become the biggest obstacle standing between Milwaukee and its own championship ambitions.
Tarik Skubal gets another opportunity to set the tone
Skubal will take the mound Sunday at American Family Field after delivering an excellent performance against the Atlanta Braves in the Division Series. The two-time Cy Young Award winner allowed one run on two hits over six innings in Game 1, striking out seven batters while issuing two walks.
Tarik Skubal will start Game 1 with Yoshinobu Yamamoto starting Game 2 for the Dodgers in the NLCS against the Brewers, per @ByJackHarris https://t.co/e8wI91D6uF
— Talkin' Baseball (@TalkinBaseball_) October 9, 2026
Los Angeles acquired Skubal from the Detroit Tigers in a blockbuster August trade, adding another established ace to an already talented pitching staff. His arrival strengthened a rotation that included Yamamoto, Blake Snell and Tyler Glasnow, giving Roberts multiple options capable of controlling a postseason game.
Starting Skubal in Game 1 is an important decision because Milwaukee owns home-field advantage in the series. The Brewers finished the regular season with 103 victories, while the Dodgers reached the 100-win mark. A strong opening performance would allow Los Angeles to immediately put pressure on a team that has been extremely difficult to beat throughout the year.
Skubal's ability to limit baserunners and generate strikeouts could be particularly valuable against a Milwaukee lineup featuring Christian Yelich, Jackson Chourio and William Contreras.
Yoshinobu Yamamoto gives Dodgers another major advantage
Yamamoto will follow Skubal in Game 2 after producing one of the Dodgers' best pitching performances against Atlanta. The right-hander struck out 10 batters over seven innings, allowing only one run on four hits in a victory that helped Los Angeles regain control of the Division Series.
The performance continued an impressive postseason history for Yamamoto, who earned World Series MVP honors in 2025. His ability to deliver deep, efficient outings gives Roberts another dependable option before the series shifts to Dodger Stadium. Milwaukee is expected to rely heavily on its own talented young pitchers, including Jacob Misiorowski and Logan Henderson. The Brewers have demonstrated throughout the season that they can compete with baseball's most talented rosters, but matching Los Angeles on the mound will be a significant challenge.
The Dodgers also have decisions remaining beyond their first two starters. Roberts indicated Friday that the team was considering adding another pitcher to its NLCS roster, a move that would require removing a position player.
Dodgers still have questions despite pitching advantage
One concern involves veteran utility player Miguel Rojas, who left Game 3 against Atlanta because of lower back discomfort. Rojas participated in baseball activities Friday, but Roberts stopped short of confirming his availability for the championship series.
The Dodgers eliminated Atlanta in four games, while Milwaukee also advanced with a four-game victory over San Diego. The teams now meet in the NLCS for the second consecutive postseason, creating another opportunity for the Brewers to challenge the defending champions. Game 1 is scheduled for Sunday at 8 p.m. ET, with Game 2 following Monday at 5 p.m. ET.
Los Angeles has plenty of offensive talent, including Shohei Ohtani, but its starting pitching could determine how this series unfolds. By sending Skubal and Yamamoto to the mound in Milwaukee, Roberts is giving the Dodgers an opportunity to establish control before returning home.

item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES -- The Dodgers' elite starting pitching was the driving force when they successfully defended their World Series title in 2025. As the back-to-back champions bid for a three-peat, their four-headed monster of a rotation has already been just as impactful four games into their postseason.
Tarik Skubal, Blake Snell, Yoshinobu Yamamoto and Tyler Glasnow recorded a combined 1.69 ERA (four earned runs in 21 1/3 innings) in four games in the NL Division Series against the Braves, the second-lowest mark among this year's postseason rotations. The Rays' starters hold a slight edge with a 1.65 ERA (three earned runs in 16 1/3 innings) in three games.
"To see it play out in the way it did was not surprising," president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman said. "But just the way they went out and competed, the way they challenged each other, we're excited for this next round and for them to get us deep into games and be a huge part of us, hopefully, winning eight more games."
As the second seed in the NL field, the Dodgers had a bye week and were able to reset their rotation to their liking for the postseason. Because they won the NLDS in four games, they'll be able to tweak their starting four again ahead of their NL Championship Series against the Brewers, which begins on Sunday at American Family Field.
With manager Dave Roberts announcing on Friday that Skubal will start Game 1 and Yamamoto Game 2, here's how the Dodgers' rotation could look through the first four games:
Skubal would have started a winner-take-all Game 5 against the Braves on Friday, but the Dodgers took care of business in four. So they'll send their big Trade Deadline reinforcement to the hill for the NLCS opener against the Brewers, who were among the other teams interested in acquiring him this summer.
Milwaukee also has yet to officially announce its rotation order, but Jacob Misiorowski appears lined up to start opposite Skubal, setting up a must-see matchup between the back-to-back AL Cy Young Award winner and this year's presumptive NL Cy Young Award winner.
The Dodgers raised eyebrows by waiting until Game 3 to start Yamamoto in the NLDS. They actually made that decision with the NLCS in mind, as Yamamoto will likely jump ahead of Snell to start Game 2 on his usual five days' rest. Yamamoto would then be available to start a potential Game 6 on his normal rest as well.
Yamamoto has never started on fewer than five days' rest with the Dodgers, but he won last year's World Series MVP honors after closing out Game 7 on zero days' rest. The right-hander said he would be open to pitching on shorter rest and/or in relief again this postseason, but L.A. will try to keep him working on his typical rest unless the situation necessitates it.
Snell showed some rust when he started NLDS Game 2, which was just his third appearance in the span of 2 1/2 weeks because of left groin tightness that flared up in mid-September. He would be working on extended rest if the Dodgers push him to Game 3, but having some more time to fine-tune his delivery might be helpful given how little he has pitched recently.
Remarkably, the Dodgers are 7-0 when Glasnow pitches in a postseason game for them. That Glasnow is the No. 4 starter in this rotation speaks to the depth of the group, as he could be the ace on many other staffs around the Majors.

item.title: [MLB.com] All signs pointing to a dream Skubal-Miz showdown for NLCS Game 1

item.content:encoded:
You get what’s shaping up to be pretty much the best pitching matchup you could ask for in Game 1 of the NL Championship Series.
The Dodgers announced Friday that Tarik Skubal will get the ball in Game 1 on Sunday, and while the Brewers haven't made anything official, they are in prime position to have ace Jacob Misiorowski on the mound. Both teams clinched their spot in the NLCS on Thursday, the Brewers with a 3-1 win over the Padres and the Dodgers with a 4-1 win over the Braves.
Misiorowski pitched just once in the series, throwing four innings of two-run ball in Game 1. Similarly, Skubal opened things against the Braves, going six innings with just one run allowed, and did not pitch again. Both should be well-rested.
The most realistic argument against a Skubal-Misiorowski duel lies in October superstar Yoshinobu Yamamoto, but the Dodgers righty pitched in Game 3 of the NLDS on Tuesday, meaning he’d start Sunday on just four days’ rest. He will pitch in Game 2 on Monday with a regular recovery that would make more sense.
We’ve seen great pitching in the 2026 postseason thus far and several marquee matchups: Cam Schlittler vs. Payton Tolle; Chris Sale vs. Jesús Luzardo; Max Fried vs. Sonny Gray; Gerrit Cole vs. Drew Rasmussen; Yamamoto vs. Sale.
If it happens, Skubal vs. Misiorowski will take the cake.
After some struggles late in the regular season, Misiorowski pitched behind an opener when he made his postseason debut a year ago, but he was effective in three appearances. He allowed only one run across seven innings in the NLDS against the Cubs, before striking out nine and yielding just one run in five innings against the Dodgers in the NLCS.
But this is not the same Miz in 2026. The flame-throwing 24-year-old finished the regular season with MLB bests in ERA (1.80), strikeouts (252), WHIP (0.80) and opponents’ batting average (.157). It was more than a breakout -- it was among the greatest pitching seasons in MLB history.
Misiorowski’s four-seam fastball topped out at 104.8 mph and averaged 101.2 mph against the Padres in the NLDS. With the adrenaline that is sure to be present on Sunday, who knows what eye-popping numbers he could put up.
As for Skubal, he won’t win a third consecutive Cy Young. But that won’t take away from the 2.72 ERA he posted in 26 starts, including a 2.61 mark after his blockbuster trade to the Dodgers. Remember, too, that Skubal missed 44 days in the summer after he needed surgery to remove loose bodies in his left elbow. There have been few signs of rust from that recovery.
Skubal’s strong playoff debut with the Dodgers was just more of what we’re used to from the southpaw. He made six postseason starts as a Tiger in 2024 and 2025 with a 2.04 ERA, never going shorter than six innings and allowing more than two runs just once.
The Brewers and Dodgers will already provide appointment viewing throughout the NLCS, a rematch of the 2025 NL pennant battle and a meeting of MLB’s top regular-season teams in 2026. Add in the potential bout of Misiorowski and Skubal in Game 1, and this series should get off to an awfully hot start.

item.content:encoded:
7일(미국 현지시간)에 열리는 내셔널리그 디비전 시리즈(NLDS) 4차전 중계 화면에 잡히는 밀워키 불펜진의 모습을 주의 깊게 지켜보시기 바랍니다.
제이콥 미시오로스키가 구원 투수로 대기하고 있는 모습을 보게 될지도 모릅니다.
팻 머피 감독은 “가능성이 있다. 충분히 그럴 수 있다”고 밝혔습니다.
6일 밤 3차전에서 패배하기는 했으나 2승 1패로 샌디에이고를 상대로 5전 3선승제 시리즈의 주도권을 여전히 쥐고 있는 밀워키에게 이번 경기가 반드시 모든 투수를 쏟아부어야 하는 총력전 상황인 것은 아닙니다. 하지만 밀워키가 이번 시리즈를 완전히 끝내기 위해 미시오로스키를 불펜 구원 투수로 투입하고도, 만약 5차전이 성사될 경우 금요일 밤 밀워키 홈에서 열릴 5차전 선발 마운드에도 그를 기용할 수 있는 시나리오는 충분히 존재합니다.
크리스 훅 투수코치는 “그는 완전히 시동이 걸려 있다”며, “나갈 준비가 되어 있다”고 강조했습니다.
마이애미 말린스는 정규시즌 막판 에이스인 샌디 알칸타라를 활용해 이와 유사한 전략을 구사한 적이 있습니다. 알칸타라는 통상적으로 선발 등판 사이 불펜 피칭을 소화해야 하는 날에 마운드에 올라 세 차례 세이브를 기록한 바 있습니다.
미시오로스키의 불펜 구원 등판 가능성에 대해 머피 감독은 “아무 이유 없이 무작정 기용하는 것은 아닐 것”이라며, “상황을 현명하게 판단하고 전후 사정을 면밀히 살펴봐야 한다. 하지만 우리 투수진의 상태는 아주 훌륭하다고 생각한다”고 설명했습니다.
밀워키는 3차전에 등판하지 않아 완벽하게 휴식을 취한 마무리 투수 트레버 메길과 셋업맨 애런 애쉬비를 보유하고 있습니다. 또한 이번 NLDS에서 아직 등판하지 않은 멀티 이닝 소화 가능한 좌완 셰인 드로한과 카일 해리슨이 대기하고 있어 선발 로버트 개서 뒤를 받쳐줄 풍부한 투수 자원을 안고 4차전에 임했습니다.
주의 깊게 지켜봐야 할 보직은 우완 셋업맨 자리일 수 있습니다. 아브너 우리베는 이번 시리즈 첫 3경기에 모두 등판했으며, 4차전에도 마운드에 오른다면 5일 동안 4번째 출전이 됩니다. 우완 안토니오 센자텔라 역시 3차전에 등판해 14개의 공을 던졌습니다.
머피 감독은 “우리 팀은 약간의 전력 노출이 있는 상태다. 양 팀 모두 서로를 너무나 잘 알고 있다”며, “그 점이 바로 이번 시리즈를 위대하게 만드는 요소 중 하나다. 다른 시리즈들은 어떻게 진행되는지 잘 모르겠다. 다른 모든 시리즈까지 챙겨보기에는 내게 너무 벅차지만, 이번 시리즈는 그야말로 믿을 수 없을 정도로 대단하다. 어느 팀이 매 경기 승리를 가져갈 자격이 있었는가? 1차전은 누가 이겼어야 했나? 2차전은 정말 그랬나? [6일 경기]는 또 어땠나? 야구란 원래 그런 법이므로, 그저 묵묵히 부딪히며 이 순간을 즐겨야 한다”고 소감을 마쳤습니다.

item.title: [Sports Illustrated] Probable Starting Pitchers for Dodgers, Braves, Brewers, Padres in NLDS Game 4
item.dc:creator: Justin Binkowski; Unknown
item.description: Following a heroic relief appearance by San Diego Padres right-hander Michael King, baseball fans will be treated to another day of four Division Series games on Wednesday. The Los Angeles Dodgers beat the Atlanta Braves 3-1 on Tuesday, while the Padres kept their postseason hopes alive with a 4-3 victory over the Milwaukee Brewers in Game 3 of the National League Division Series. All four teams will be back in action on Wednesday, with San Diego and Atlanta needing a win to stay in the 2026 MLB
item.content:encoded:
Following a heroic relief appearance by San Diego Padres right-hander Michael King, baseball fans will be treated to another day of four Division Series games on Wednesday.
The Los Angeles Dodgers beat the Atlanta Braves 3-1 on Tuesday, while the Padres kept their postseason hopes alive with a 4-3 victory over the Milwaukee Brewers in Game 3 of the National League Division Series. All four teams will be back in action on Wednesday, with San Diego and Atlanta needing a win to stay in the 2026 MLB playoffs.
Here are the expected starting pitching matchups for Game 4 in each NLDS.
Braves vs. Dodgers
Los Angeles right-hander Yoshinobu Yamamoto delivered another dominant postseason performance on Tuesday, tossing seven innings of one-run ball and striking out 10. With a 2-1 series lead, the Dodgers will now give the ball to another All-Star hurler.
Right-hander Tyler Glasnow will start for Los Angeles in Game 4. The 6-foot-8 righty will make his first playoff appearance of the season on Wednesday after being limited to 13 regular-season starts. But the hard-throwing hurler still had a 3.53 ERA and 98 strikeouts in 74 innings this year. In his career, the 33-year-old has a 4.43 ERA in 16 postseason games (13 starts).
With Atlanta's season on the line, right-hander Tyler Mahle is starting Game 4. The 32-year-old made his MLB postseason debut in the Braves' Wild Card Series matchup with the Philadelphia Phillies, throwing seven innings and allowing just one run. The veteran will try to keep the Dodgers' bats at bay to force a winner-take-all Game 5.
Brewers vs. Padres
With the Padres facing elimination, King pitched the last two innings of Game 3 after starting Game 2. Relievers Mason Miller and Adrian Morejon were unavailable on Tuesday, so Robbie Ray and Joe Musgrove were warming up in the bullpen during the ninth inning of Game 3. With that in mind, San Diego will likely have all hands on deck in Game 4.
The Padres will start right-hander Walker Buehler on Wednesday. The 32-year-old has plenty of postseason experience, posting a 3.04 ERA in 19 career playoff games. But it'll be interesting to see how long of a leash the veteran has in a must-win game for San Diego.
Meanwhile, left-hander Robert Gasser is expected to start Game 4 for the Brewers. The 27-year-old will make his first postseason start after pitching in two games out of the bullpen in the 2025 playoffs. Most notably, though, Gasser starting on Wednesday sets the stage for Jacob Misiorowski to either pitch in the late innings of Game 4 or start Game 5 for Milwaukee if necessary.
Justin Binkowski is a lifelong baseball fan returning to cover the sport he loves after spending nearly a decade writing about video games. Before his time as managing editor at Dot Esports, Binkowski attended King's College in Wilkes-Barre, PA, where he was also a relief pitcher on the school's baseball team. While in college, Binkowski was a media relations intern for the Scranton/Wilkes-Barre RailRiders during the 2014 season.
Follow JBinkk

item.title: [The New York Times] MLB playoff games today: Saturday’s schedule, times, TV channels, streaming and starters

item.content:encoded:
The Athletic has live coverage of the MLB Playoffs, including the ALDS Game 2s of White Sox vs Guardians and Yankees vs Rays.
After three days of Wild Card Series action, the dust has settled and four teams (Houston Astros, Boston Red Sox, Philadelphia Phillies and Chicago Cubs) have found themselves on an early vacation. Major League Baseball’s 12-team postseason field has been whittled to eight.
Now, the race for the World Series shifts to the next round: the Division Series. Four teams (Cleveland Guardians, Los Angeles Dodgers, Tampa Bay Rays and Milwaukee Brewers) that had first-round byes will now be in action. Additionally, while the Wild Card Series featured a best-of-three format, the Division Series will be best-of-five.
Here’s how MLB’s bracket looks right now:
You can watch the MLB playoffs on Fubo (Stream Free Now).
What is Saturday’s MLB Playoff schedule and starters?
White Sox at Guardians (AL Division Series Game 1): Hagen Smith vs. Parker Messick
First pitch: 1 p.m. ET (TBS)
After the 23-year-old Smith pitched three scoreless innings in Game 1 of the Wild Card Series against the Astros, the White Sox turn to him for an encore performance in Game 1 of the ALDS. While the club was able to pile on six runs against the Astros in a win, it won’t be as easy against the Guardians and Messick.
An All-Star this season, Messick finished his rookie campaign with a 2.56 ERA and 193 strikeouts over 32 starts. Against the White Sox, Messick carded a 2.81 ERA in four starts (25 2/3 innings).
Braves at Dodgers (NL Division Series Game 1): TBD vs. Tarik Skubal
First pitch: 4 p.m. ET (Fox)
Having burned Chris Sale to take Thursday’s winner-take-all game against the Phillies, and with Tyler Mahle also unavailable, the Braves appear to be looking at another bullpen game.
“They’ve pitched in big situations during the season, and no matter who we really see right now in that bullpen in any situation, no matter what inning it is, we’re feeling pretty confident about them,” catcher Drake Baldwin told reporters.
The Dodgers, coming off a first-round bye, will counter with Tarik Skubal, the crown jewel acquisition of this year’s trade deadline. The AL’s reigning Cy Young Award winner has a 2.61 ERA with his new team, his final starts before reaching a highly anticipated free agency.
Yankees at Rays (AL Division Series Game 1): Gerrit Cole vs. Drew Rasmussen
First pitch: 6:30 p.m. ET (TBS)
Faced with an embarrassment of riches on the pitching side, the Yankees will deploy 2023 AL Cy Young Award winner Gerrit Cole against the AL East champs. After Cole in Game 1, the Yankees will have Cam Schlittler in Game 2 and some variation of Max Fried or Carlos Rodón in Games 3 and 4, the last matchup only if necessary.
On the Tampa Bay side, Drew Rasmussen, arguably one of the most underrated aces in the sport, will get the ball at Tropicana Field. For his career, Rasmussen has a 1.81 ERA in 11 games (10 starts) against the Yankees.
Padres at Brewers (NL Division Series Game 1): Robbie Ray vs. Jacob Misiorowski
First pitch: 8:30 p.m. ET (FS1)
Saturday’s final matchup will feature two pitchers at opposite ends of their careers. On the San Diego side, Robbie Ray, the 2021 AL Cy Young Award winner, has been largely unable to replicate the success he had that season. After a deadline trade from the San Francisco Giants to the Padres, Ray has carded a 5.02 ERA over nine starts.
For the Brewers, Jacob Misiorowski is just getting started. An All-Star in his rookie year, Misiorowski finished his sophomore campaign as the favorite to win the NL Cy Young Award, leading MLB with a 1.80 ERA and 252 strikeouts. He’s wowed the sport with his ability to repeatedly fire fastballs in excess of 100 mph, and there’s reason to believe that, at 24 years old, his best is yet to come.
What to know about each Division Series matchup
White Sox at Guardians: The two AL Central clubs played each other 13 times during the regular season, with the White Sox winning the season series 7-6. That, however, was not enough to overcome a late surge by the Guardians and a collapse by Chicago that led to the White Sox losing control of the division and having to play their way out of the wild card.
Now, the two clubs will meet again for at least three games, a spot in the Championship Series on the line. By winning the division and finishing with a better record than the AL West winner, the Guardians were granted a first-round bye. No mind, the White Sox dispatched the Astros in two games and have been off since Thursday. That extra rest has allowed the club to realign its depleted pitching staff.
One thing to watch: How Chicago’s thin, matchup-dependent pitching staff is deployed against Cleveland’s newfound offense — the club led the AL in wRC+ (108) from Aug. 1 onward. The urgency, or lack thereof, by White Sox manager Will Venable could swing the series either direction.
Braves at Dodgers: The Braves’ pitching staff will enter Game 1 with very little margin for error, as it will likely be a group effort without a starter available. That alone could be the difference, as teams that take Game 1 in any best-of-five series have historically won the series 72 percent of the time. That said, these Dodgers have not played their best against the Braves, losing the season series 5-1, including a late-August sweep when Tyler Glasnow and Yoshinobu Yamamoto both pitched.
One thing to watch: Shohei Ohtani’s ability to contribute. The four-time MVP has spent much of the second half of the season compromised, leading to an abbreviated September, with some of it on the injured list.
“I do feel like my swing is in a better place, feels smooth, and just a little tweaks here and there, and I’ll be ready for tomorrow,” Ohtani said through interpreter Will Ireton.
Yankees at Rays: Only one team had a better record over its final 30 games than the Rays, who went 20-10 to fend off a late Yankees push to claim the AL East. That, plus a 55-26 home record that tied the Brewers for the best in MLB, has Tampa Bay inching toward its first World Series appearance since 2020. To get there, the Rays will need to beat the Yankees, who made quick work of the Red Sox in the wild-card round. That they did so without Aaron Judge on the roster or needing to call on Giancarlo Stanton in a pinch hit capacity is all the more impressive.
One thing to watch: Junior Caminero was 20 years old the last time the Rays made the postseason, going hitless in two at-bats. Since then, Caminero, now 23, has morphed into a perennial All-Star, hitting 40 home runs in consecutive seasons, the latter of which should earn him major MVP consideration. Few players love the big stage as much as Caminero. One of those players just so happens to be Cam Schlittler, the presumptive AL Cy Young Award winner, who will take the ball at least once this series. How these two match up will be one of the best subplots of this postseason.
Padres at Brewers: In a battle between arguably MLB’s hottest team (the Padres) and the league’s best team all season (the Brewers), there will be a lot of firsts. This is San Diego’s first Division Series under new owners José E. Feliciano and his wife and business partner Kwanza Jones. It will be the first extended runway for Padres rookie catcher Ethan Salas. It will be the first postseason series for Christian Yelich as the Brewers’ captain. And it will be the first time Misiorowski faces these Padres since May.
Should Milwaukee win, it will be the first time in franchise history that the club has made it to back-to-back league championship series. If San Diego upsets MLB’s No. 1 team, it will be the club’s first trip since 2022 and just its fourth overall.
One thing to watch: The bullpens. Behind multiple high-leverage arms, San Diego has made the late innings nearly impossible for opposing teams. If there’s one club that can match the Padres in that regard, it’s the Brewers. The late innings will likely be the deciding factor in who advances.

item.title: [NBC Sports] 2026 Fantasy baseball league winners: Jacob Misiorowski, Jordan Walker, Miguel Vargas, more
item.dc:creator: Eric Samulski
item.description: We’ve had some time for the dust to settle on the 2026 fantasy baseball season, which means it’s time to look back on what we learned (or should have learned) before we turn the page to 2027. item.content:encoded:
We’ve had some time for the dust to settle on the 2026 fantasy baseball season, which means it’s time to look back on what we learned (or should have learned) before we turn the page to 2027. I figured I’d start by looking at “league winners.”
We love to throw the term “league winner” around, but what does it really mean? I could have looked at all the teams who won leagues and found the players who appeared on most of them. That would be valid, but I don’t have all that data at my fingertips, and I believe the players who “won” you something were the players who outproduced their acquisition cost by the most. So that’s what I looked at: which players produced the most fantasy value based on what it cost to get them. Which players gave you the biggest return on investment. Chances are, if you hit on one or more of these guys, you were in for a pretty solid season.
To measure what their return on investment was, I took the FanGraphs Player Rater dollar values for 12-team leagues and used the Player Rater’s ADP, which is derived from NFBC formats. I compared what each player earned with what his draft position should have earned. The “should have earned” part, I needed some help with, so I had Claude average the 2026 earnings of every player drafted within a reasonable range (about 22%) of the ADP for that pick. So, for example, if the player was the 100th pick, I looked at the value produced by players drafted 78th through 128th. That felt like a fair way to say, “this pick should have produced a value around this amount.”
I referred to that below as their “Slot Cost.” Every pick after pick 250, I also treated as a waiver wire add, which meant it cost nothing to acquire the player. By taking the final dollar value for each player and subtracting their slot cost, we’re left with the players who earned far more than it cost to draft/acquire them.
So who were those players in 2026?
2026 Fantasy Baseball League-Winning Hitters
| Player | Pos | 2026 ADP | Slot cost | 2026 $ | Profit vs slot |
| Pete Crow-Armstrong | OF | 33 | $14.1 | $49.5 | +$35.5 |
| Jordan Walker | OF | 512 | $0.0 | $29.4 | +$29.4 |
| Ben Rice | C/1B/DH | 53 | $9.7 | $36.6 | +$26.9 |
| Miguel Vargas | 1B/3B | 303 | $0.0 | $26.5 | +$26.5 |
| Otto Lopez | 2B/SS | 229 | $0.0 | $26.5 | +$26.5 |
| CJ Abrams | SS | 65 | $9.1 | $33.9 | +$24.8 |
| Sal Stewart | 1B/3B | 162 | $3.3 | $27.9 | +$24.6 |
| Jake McCarthy | OF | 507 | $0.0 | $24.4 | +$24.4 |
| Gabriel Moreno | C/DH | 181 | $0.4 | $24.2 | +$23.8 |
| Alec Burleson | 1B/OF/DH | 175 | $0.9 | $23.9 | +$23.0 |
Not a ton of surprises here. Even though Pete Crow-Armstrong was a top 40 pick, he still vastly outperformed his draft slot. His production so far has exceeded everyone else’s, so he was the ultimate “league winner.” Ben Rice and CJ Abrams were also early-round picks who returned far more than it cost to acquire them, keeping in mind that Rice is catcher-eligible and this is for two-catcher formats.
PCA, Rice, and Abrams also join a group of hitters here who were already pretty good in 2025. Alec Burleson, Miguel Vargas, and Otto Lopez all had flashed usable production in 2025 and were locked into full-time roles. We may not have seen this jump coming, but we likely could have been drafting them higher based on underlying skills and roles.
We have talked ad nauseuam about Jordan Walker‘s breakout and ways in which we could have seen it coming. Sal Stewart was a highly touted rookie who delivered in his first full season, while both Gabriel Moreno and Jake McCarthy earned far more playing time than they were projected to. Moreno had never had more than 380 plate appearances in a season, but had 550 this year, and McCarthy won a starting job in Colorado, which also made him our staff vote for comeback player of the year.
Some other waiver wire players (ADP after pick 250) who came close to making this list were: Dillon Dingler ($22 value in 2026), Liam Hicks ($22), Jake Bauers ($20.8), Carter Jensen ($18.8), Luis Garcia Jr. ($18.6), Kevin McGonigle ($17.8), Carson Benge ($17.8), and Brooks Lee ($14.1).
2026 Fantasy Baseball League-Winning Pitchers
| Player | Pos | 2026 ADP | Slot cost | 2026 $ | Profit vs slot |
| Jacob Misiorowski | SP | 114 | $6.3 | $41.7 | +$35.4 |
| Cam Schlittler | SP | 117 | $5.2 | $37.6 | +$32.4 |
| Drew Rasmussen | SP | 132 | $4.9 | $28.9 | +$24.0 |
| Parker Messick | SP | 294 | $0.0 | $23.0 | +$23.0 |
| Jacob Latz | SP/RP | 731 | $0.0 | $17.6 | +$17.6 |
| Logan Henderson | SP | 413 | $0.0 | $17.4 | +$17.4 |
| Cade Cavalli | SP | 305 | $0.0 | $16.5 | +$16.5 |
| Nick Martinez | SP | 738 | $0.0 | $16.4 | +$16.4 |
| Dylan Cease | SP | 75 | $7.9 | $23.6 | +$15.7 |
| Yoshinobu Yamamoto | SP | 27 | $15.2 | $30.7 | +$15.6 |
Again, we start the list with names that are not particularly surprising. Jacob Misiorowski and Cam Schlittler were the best two pitchers in the league this season, and neither one of them was drafted inside the top 100 picks. Yoshinobu Yamamoto and Dylan Cease were the only two other semi-highly drafted pitchers who produced a “league-winning” return on your investment. I guess we can include Drew Rasmussen in there too.
Of this group of ten pitchers, five of them (Misiorowski, Schlittler, Logan Henderson, Parker Messick, and Cade Cavalli) were high strikeout rate arms who didn’t pitch enough innings in 2025 to be among the top arms drafted. In fairness to drafters, Parker Messick wasn’t officially in the rotation until the end of May, and Cade Cavalli was fairly mediocre until a pitch mix change and velocity bump in the middle of June. Still, betting on strikeout arms coming off limited workload makes sense.
The majority of the other names on here had a clear role/situation change. Drew Rasmussen was another year removed from injury and went up over 170 innings. Nick Martinez was given a chance to be a full-time starter, Jacob Latz was turned into a closer, and Dylan Cease changed organizations, which led to massive improvement from his changeup and attack plan.
So who could fit this bill in 2027?
Potential League-Winning Hitters in 2027
| Player | Pos | 2026 age | 2026 PA | Barrel % | 2026 $ |
| Heriberto Hernández | OF/DH | 26 | 505 | 12.7 | $4.1 |
| Spencer Torkelson | 1B | 26 | 612 | 12.2 | $6.0 |
| Colson Montgomery | 3B/SS | 24 | 638 | 12 | $7.6 |
| Munetaka Murakami | 1B | 26 | 553 | 20.5 | $9.1 |
| Chase DeLauter | OF/DH | 24 | 559 | 6.3 | $10.5 |
| Jac Caglianone | 1B/OF | 23 | 553 | 13 | $14.2 |
| Riley Greene | OF/DH | 25 | 592 | 14.8 | $14.6 |
| Garrett Mitchell | OF | 27 | 531 | 11.7 | $8.3 |
| Wilyer Abreu | OF | 27 | 681 | 12.5 | $13.2 |
| Luis García Jr. | 1B/2B | 26 | 543 | 12.2 | $18.6 |
If we’re going to identify who were league winners in 2026, then it makes sense to use that information to project who would be a league winner in 2027. The hitters who made the league winner list seemed to fall into two categories: Players who had already shown flashes of success and were underpriced (Rice, Burleson, Vargas, PCA, Lopez) and players who experienced a significant bump in playing time from the previous season (Walker, Stewart, McCarthy, Moreno).
It’s hard to use 2026 numbers to project who will have a playing time boost in 2027, so I’ll leave that part to the side for now. To find potentially underpriced hitters, I wanted to look at the commonalities behind the hitters who were “league winners” this year. Among all qualified hitters, having a 12%+ barrel rate or a 91+ mph average exit velocity, combined with being age 26 or younger, doubled the rate of $10+ profits returned. Meanwhile, strikeout rate, walk rate, chase rate, and swinging-strike rate had no relationship to profit.
That means, if we’re looking for players to break out in 2027, we should be looking for players entering their athletic prime who hit the ball hard. Not a shocking revelation, and I already write an off-season column about hitters entering their athletic prime years. This year, that column mentioned Rice, Vargas, Lopez, Ryan Jeffers, Wilyer Abreu, Alejandro Kirk, and a collection of hitters who did not break out (Brett Baty, Heliot Ramos, Andrew Vaughn, etc.)
In addition to the list above, there are a few players who fit the hard contact and age profile but will likely already be priced up by the market. I’m not going to list them as potential league winners, but they should be targets for you in drafts, even at cost: Walker, Stewart, Vargas, Drake Baldwin, Hunter Goodman, Carter Jensen, James Wood and Jackson Chourio. All earned $18–30 this season and could see a sizeable boost from that in 2027.
Of the others listed, Jac Caglianone might be the best fit based on age and his 13% barrel rate and 93.3 mph average exit velocity. We already know why Riley Greene is an exciting fantasy option, but he produced just $15 of value in 2026. There’s a path for him to be a $30+ guy. Heriberto Hernandez and Chase DeLauter could take big steps forward with more playing time; Luis Garcia Jr. has a full season in Yankee Stadium, and all of Spencer Torkelson, Munetaka Murakami, and Colson Montgomery have the batted ball quality but major contact issues. If they can make strides in their contact rates, their power could lead to a massive return on investment for fantasy.
Potential League-Winning Pitchers in 2027
| Player | Team | Pos | 2026 IP | K/IP | 2026 $ |
| Didier Fuentes | ATL | SP/RP | 73.1 | 1.26 | $9.1 |
| Jonah Tong | NYM | SP | 30.2 | 1.13 | -$3.6 |
| Tatsuya Imai | HOU | SP | 76.2 | 1.27 | -$7.3 |
| Gage Jump | ATH | SP | 98.2 | 1.10 | -$15.4 |
| Brandon Sproat | MIL | SP | 97.0 | 1.04 | -$16.3 |
| Jack Leiter | TEX | SP | 80.0 | 1.04 | -$12.8 |
| Jackson Jobe | DET | SP | 46.0 | 1.11 | -$2.1 |
| Mason Montgomery | PIT | SP/RP | 68.2 | 1.54 | $13.3 |
| Grant Taylor | CHW | SP/RP | 84.0 | 1.26 | $13.8 |
Looking at the starting pitchers who made our “league-winners” list earlier in the article, the key is strikeouts. Among all starters drafted at an ADP between 90–400, those who threw under 100 innings in 2025 and posted a 1.0 K/IP or higher averaged $4.40 or more when compared to their slot, and 31% of them returned $10+ profit. So we need to be looking for starting pitchers like that. The names that came up were Didier Fuentes, Jonah Tong, and Logan Henderson. Of course, Henderson already was a “league-winner” in 2026, so his price will be high.
Younger pitchers who had the strikeouts but a poor ERA also fit the bill. Remember that Misiorowski had a 4.36 ERA in 2025. He was missing tons of bats, but the surface-level ratios weren’t ideal. Pitchers like Tatsuya Imai, Brandon Sproat, Jackson Jobe, and Jack Leiter all fit the bill. So did Gage Jump and Mason Barnett, but factoring in the element of pitching in Sacramento muddies those waters.
The other names on this list, Mason Montgomery and Grant Taylor, are either elite closers or potentially breakout starters if they’re moved back into the rotation. There is obviously a lot of uncertainty with their roles in 2027, but they are names to keep an eye on, especially if we have a better idea of their role.

item.title: [Bleacher Report] Ranking Every MLB Playoff Team's Projected 2026 Postseason Rotation
item.dc:creator: Joel Reuter
item.description: Ranking Every MLB Playoff Team's Projected 2026 Postseason Rotation Pitching wins championships. item.content:encoded:
Ranking Every MLB Playoff Team's Projected 2026 Postseason Rotation
Pitching wins championships.
While that old adage still holds true, it has taken on a slightly different meaning in today's game, as teams need to successfully utilize their entire pitching staff to make a deep playoff run, rather than simply leaning on two or three starting pitchers to shoulder the load.
Still, a strong performance from the starting staff can give a team a major leg up. The Los Angeles Dodgers were the perfect example of that last October.
Ahead, we've ranked the playoff rotations of every postseason team. Which team's rotation is best positioned heading into the playoffs?
12. Houston Astros
1 of 12
RHP Hunter Brown (6-3, 3.26 ERA, 1.28 WHIP, 120 K, 102.0 IP)
RHP Hayden Wesneski (5-2, 3.50 ERA, 1.15 WHIP, 41 K, 54.0 IP)
RHP Peter Lambert (8-10, 3.87 ERA, 1.26 WHIP, 153 K, 153.2 IP)
RHP Ethan Pecko (1-0, 4.31 ERA, 1.21 WHIP, 21 K, 31.1 IP)
Other Candidates: RHP Ronel Blanco, RHP Cristian Javier (out for ALWC)
The Astros have used 19 different starting pitchers this year while navigating a long list of injuries. The fact that reliever AJ Blubaugh ranks third on the team with 95.1 innings pitched speaks volumes.
Ace Hunter Brown was slowed by a shoulder strain in the first half of the season, but he has returned to form with a 3.11 ERA and 81 strikeouts in 66.2 innings since the All-Star break.
With Cristian Javier making an early exit from his start on Wednesday, the rotation behind Brown is entirely up in the air. Hayden Wesneski and Peter Lambert are both capable of tossing a quality start, but they are short on big-game experience and could also be susceptible to a quick hook, shifting the focus to a Houston bullpen that ranks 17th in the majors with a 4.09 ERA.
11. Chicago White Sox
2 of 12
RHP Sean Burke (10-7, 3.40 ERA, 1.20 WHIP, 178 K, 167.0 IP)
RHP Davis Martin (9-7, 3.84 ERA, 1.29 WHIP, 121 K, 145.1 IP)
RHP Erick Fedde (8-9, 3.83 ERA, 1.36 WHIP, 99 K, 141.0 IP)
LHP Anthony Kay (9-9, 4.53 ERA, 1.37 WHIP, 125 K, 153.0 IP)
Other Candidates: RHP Luis Castillo, RHP David Sandlin
The White Sox rank 26th in starters' ERA (4.62) and 28th in quality starts (34), so the starting rotation is something they will need to figure out how to navigate in the postseason rather than a strength.
Sean Burke and Davis Martin have accounted for 21 of those 33 quality starts. They will be asked to chew up innings at the top of the rotation, while games outside of their starts will likely be an all-hands-on-deck situation.
Sean Newcomb (58 G, 6 GS, 3.17 ERA, 88.0 IP) and Grant Taylor (59 G, 4 GS, 2.30 ERA, 82.0 IP) are both capable of providing length out of the bullpen, while deadline pickup Luis Castillo has also been shifted to a relief role.
10. Chicago Cubs
3 of 12
LHP Shota Imanaga (11-10, 3.74 ERA, 1.10 WHIP, 171 K, 173.1 IP)
RHP Kevin Gausman (4-2, 4.83 ERA, 1.23 WHIP, 57 K, 50.1 IP)
LHP Matthew Boyd (10-5, 3.91 ERA, 1.21 WHIP, 96 K, 126.2 IP)
LHP David Peterson (6-2, 3.94 ERA, 1.39 WHIP, 68 K, 75.1 IP)
Other Candidates: RHP Clay Holmes, RHP Javier Assad
The Cubs roll into October with arguably the best offense and best defense in baseball, but questions about their pitching staff hang over their postseason outlook.
Shota Imanaga has a 1.96 ERA and a 23-to-2 strikeout-to-walk ratio over 23 innings in September. That should put him in line to be the ace of the staff in October.
Veteran Kevin Gausman's significant playoff experience, including starting Game 2 and Game 6 of the World Series a year ago, should earn him a prominent role in the playoffs. At the back of the staff, Clay Holmes is the obvious candidate to shift to the bullpen given his past experience closing games.
9. San Diego Padres
4 of 12
RHP Michael King (12-10, 3.21 ERA, 1.18 WHIP, 159 K, 185.0 IP)
RHP Nick Pivetta (3-2, 2.86 ERA, 1.01 WHIP, 42 K, 34.2 IP)
RHP Walker Buehler (9-6, 4.56 ERA, 1.34 WHIP, 128 K, 150.0 IP)
LHP Robbie Ray (3-2, 5.02 ERA, 1.54 WHIP, 33 K, 43.0 IP)
Other Candidates: RHP Casey Mize, RHP Randy Vásquez
The Padres rank fourth in the majors and top among projected playoff teams with 666.0 innings of work from their bullpen. That relief corps, anchored by Mason Miller and Adrian Morejón, will be a major factor in October.
Michael King is the clear ace of the staff. Nick Pivetta has pitched well since returning on Sept. 7, with 11 hits and three earned runs allowed in 14 innings over three starts.
Behind them, Walker Buehler is the logical Game 3 candidate, given his postseason resume and 3.15 ERA over 45.2 innings in his last nine starts. Deadline pickups Robbie Ray and Casey Mize have struggled since coming to San Diego and could be X-factors if they advance beyond the Wild Card Round.
8. Cleveland Guardians
5 of 12
RHP Gavin Williams (14-8, 3.63 ERA, 1.08 WHIP, 244 K, 181.0 IP)
LHP Parker Messick (12-9, 2.55 ERA, 1.04 WHIP, 191 K, 183.1 IP)
RHP Tanner Bibee (6-15, 4.35 ERA, 1.22 WHIP, 142 K, 182.0 IP)
LHP Joey Cantillo (11-9, 3.62 ERA, 1.42 WHIP, 171 K, 159.0 IP)
Other Candidates: LHP Foster Griffin
Gavin Williams leads the AL with 244 strikeouts and Parker Messick has a 2.27 ERA in 71.1 innings since the All-Star break, giving the Guardians a legitimate one-two punch to lead the way in the postseason.
Opening Day starter Tanner Bibee has struggled, posting an 8.24 ERA over 19.2 innings in September, but his track record still makes him the most likely candidate to start Game 3.
The question then becomes who gets the nod between Foster Griffin and Joey Cantillo. Griffin has a 5.19 ERA in nine starts since he was acquired at the trade deadline, while Cantillo has better surface-level results but has issued an AL-leading 81 walks in 159 innings.
7. Atlanta Braves
6 of 12
LHP Chris Sale (14-9, 2.16 ERA, 0.98 WHIP, 200 K, 162.2 IP)
RHP Tyler Mahle (4-1, 1.99 ERA, 0.96 WHIP, 48 K, 54.1 IP)
RHP Grant Holmes (10-5, 3.47 ERA, 1.30 WHIP, 114 K, 147.2 IP)
RHP JR Ritchie (1-4, 4.79 ERA, 1.46 WHIP, 66 K, 67.2 IP)
Other Candidates: RHP Bryce Elder, RHP AJ Smith-Shawver, LHP Martín Pérez (out for NLWC)
Starting pitching was expected to be a glaring issue for the Braves when Spencer Strider, Spencer Schwellenbach, Hurston Waldrep and AJ Smith-Shawver all began the season on the injured list.
Instead, Chris Sale has put together a Cy Young-caliber season, while journeyman veterans Martín Pérez and Grant Holmes have combined for a 3.26 ERA in 289.2 innings spanning 55 starts. However, Pérez was just placed on the injured list with lower back inflammation, making a bullpen game the likely approach to fill the fourth starter role if they advance to the NLDS.
Deadline pickup Tyler Mahle has given them the No. 2 starter they still lacked, while a healthy Bryce Elder could be an X-factor if they advance deeper into October.
6. Milwaukee Brewers
7 of 12
RHP Jacob Misiorowski (15-5, 1.86 ERA, 0.80 WHIP, 247 K, 169.1 IP)
RHP Logan Henderson (11-3, 2.47 ERA, 0.84 WHIP, 110 K, 98.1 IP)
LHP Robert Gasser (5-5, 4.01 ERA, 1.24 WHIP, 94 K, 103.1 IP)
RHP Dustin May (2-2, 5.61 ERA, 1.43 WHIP, 33 K, 33.2 IP)
Other Candidates: LHP Kyle Harrison, LHP Shane Drohan
Jacob Misiorowski pitched out of the bullpen for the Brewers last October, posting a 1.50 ERA, 0.83 WHIP and 16 strikeouts in 12 innings across three appearances. He is now poised to lead their staff this postseason.
Rookie Logan Henderson has not allowed more than three earned runs in any of his 18 starts this season. He is 8-2 with a 2.19 ERA and 0.79 WHIP in 70 innings since the All-Star break.
Left-hander Robert Gasser has a 1.71 ERA in 26.1 innings over his last five appearances. He will be a significant part of manager Pat Murphy's plan of mixing and matching innings behind Misiorowski and Henderson.
5. Boston Red Sox
8 of 12
RHP Sonny Gray (18-5, 2.72 ERA, 1.15 WHIP, 149 K, 169.0 IP)
LHP Ranger Suarez (8-5, 3.22 ERA, 1.19 WHIP, 140 K, 148.1 IP)
LHP Payton Tolle (9-6, 3.03 ERA, 1.10 WHIP, 171 K, 148.2 IP)
RHP Brayan Bello (6-7, 4.49 ERA, 1.37 WHIP, 90 K, 112.1 IP)
Other Candidates: LHP Jake Bennett, LHP Patrick Sandoval
Few offseason additions have made a bigger impact than Sonny Gray, who has 20 quality starts in 29 games this year and is on track for his fourth career top-10 finish in Cy Young voting for four different teams.
Rookie Payton Tolle has been the team's most consistent starter behind Gray this year and will factor into the playoff rotation, while high-priced offseason signing Ranger Suarez has a 1.09 ERA over 24.2 innings in September.
The X-factor could be Brayan Bello after he threw a gem (8.0 IP, 5 H, 1 ER, 11 K) on the road against the Rays on Sept. 19. He has a 2.28 ERA over 51.1 innings while working mostly out of the bullpen since returning from a minor league demotion before the All-Star break, but he is stretched back out to start.
4. Tampa Bay Rays
9 of 12
RHP Drew Rasmussen (16-5, 2.67 ERA, 0.91 WHIP, 174 K, 172.0 IP)
RHP Nick Martinez (15-5, 2.94 ERA, 1.07 WHIP, 108 K, 177.1 IP)
RHP Freddy Peralta (4-2, 3.60 ERA, 0.98 WHIP, 39 K, 50.0 IP)
RHP Griffin Jax (8-10, 3.62 ERA, 1.19 WHIP, 115 K, 109.1 IP)
Other Candidates: LHP Ian Seymour, LHP Shane McClanahan (out for ALDS)
Few organizations do a better job fully utilizing the entire pitching staff than the Rays, but this October they have three legitimate rotation anchors who can get them deep into games in Drew Rasmussen, Nick Martinez and deadline pickup Freddy Peralta.
That group gets even deeper if Shane McClanahan returns to action, though he has already been ruled out for the ALDS. Even if he's not able to return, reliever-turned-starter Griffin Jax has also been quietly excellent this season with a 3.23 ERA and 105 strikeouts in 100.1 innings over his 22 starts.
They could still opt to utilize an opener when it makes sense, or piggyback one of their starters with left-hander Ian Seymour if the situation arises. This isn't a staff that needs to lean on multiple bullpen games to get through a series.
3. Philadelphia Phillies
10 of 12
LHP Cristopher Sánchez (18-6, 2.93 ERA, 1.22 WHIP, 221 K, 200.0 IP)
RHP Zack Wheeler (13-5, 3.06 ERA, 1.06 WHIP, 188 K, 156.0 IP)
RHP Aaron Nola (7-11, 4.54 ERA, 1.33 WHIP, 177 K, 174.1 IP)
LHP Jesús Luzardo (14-5, 2.87 ERA, 1.08 WHIP, 221 K, 178.2 IP)
Other Candidates: RHP Andrew Painter
Jesús Luzardo played catch earlier this week as he works his way back from shoulder inflammation, though his postseason status remains up in the air. There's a chance he will be limited to bullpen work early in the playoffs.
Veteran Aaron Nola has hit his stride of late, posting a 2.45 ERA in 66 innings over his last 11 starts, so he can fill the void behind the dynamic one-two punch of Cristopher Sánchez (7.7 WAR, 1st among all SP) and Zack Wheeler (5.6 WAR, 8th among all SP).
The Phillies rank second in the majors with 73 quality starts and 869.1 innings from their starting staff, so they are poised to lean on their starters as hard as anyone in October.
2. New York Yankees
11 of 12
RHP Cam Schlittler (14-6, 1.95 ERA, 0.92 WHIP, 239 K, 193.2 IP)
LHP Max Fried (5-5, 2.80 ERA, 0.99 WHIP, 104 K, 112.2 IP)
RHP Gerrit Cole (10-9, 3.61 ERA, 1.10 WHIP, 131 K, 127.0 IP)
LHP Carlos Rodón (7-3, 2.67 ERA, 1.06 WHIP, 91 K, 84.1 IP)
Other Candidates: RHP Will Warren
With AL Cy Young favorite Cam Schlittler and three established veteran starters capable of frontline production in Max Fried, Gerrit Cole and Carlos Rodón, the Yankees rotation is capable of making a major impact in October.
Schlittler logged a 1.26 ERA over 14.1 innings last October, including eight scoreless frames against the rival Red Sox in the Wild Card Round. He will now be asked to shoulder a heavier load.
It remains to be seen who the odd-man out would be in a series that calls for a three-man staff, though Rodón has made his case with a 1.42 ERA, 0.75 WHIP and 28 strikeouts in 25.1 innings in September.
1. Los Angeles Dodgers
12 of 12
RHP Yoshinobu Yamamoto (14-9, 2.53 ERA, 0.87 WHIP, 182 K, 185.0 IP)
LHP Tarik Skubal (4-2, 2.95 ERA, 1.13 WHIP, 60 K, 55.0 IP)
LHP Blake Snell (4-1, 1.86 ERA, 1.09 WHIP, 52 K, 38.2 IP)
RHP Tyler Glasnow (5-2, 3.53 ERA, 0.95 WHIP, 98 K, 74.0 IP)
Other Candidates: RHP Emmet Sheehan, LHP Justin Wrobleski
The Dodgers have once again navigated much of the regular season without Blake Snell and Tyler Glasnow, but they are healthy rolling into October and poised to round out the playoff rotation alongside Yoshinobu Yamamoto and deadline pickup Tarik Skubal.
The starting rotation logged a 2.68 ERA over 104 innings last postseason, with Yamamoto, Snell and Glasnow starting 13 of 17 games and the rest going to Shohei Ohtani, who will be limited to DH duties but has been sufficiently replaced by a two-time Cy Young winner in Skubal.
Right-hander Emmet Sheehan has a 0.53 ERA and 24 strikeouts over 17 innings in three September starts. He will serve as a multi-inning weapon out of the bullpen.

item.title: [MLB.com] Here's how the pitching might line up for the White Sox-Guardians ALDS
item.dc:creator: Tim Stebbins; Scott Merkin
item.description: CLEVELAND -- While battling for the American League Central title last month, the Guardians and White Sox divisional race featured an added reward: a first-round bye in the postseason that would allow the champ to set its preferred pitching plan for the AL Division Series. That’s where we find ourselves now, as Cleveland and Chicago get set for their first-ever playoff matchup. item.content:encoded:
CLEVELAND -- While battling for the American League Central title last month, the Guardians and White Sox divisional race featured an added reward: a first-round bye in the postseason that would allow the champ to set its preferred pitching plan for the AL Division Series.
That’s where we find ourselves now, as Cleveland and Chicago get set for their first-ever playoff matchup.
As the AL Central champion Guardians enjoyed a bye this week, they also lined up their staff anchors for the first two games of ALDS, which is set to kick off with Game 1 on Saturday at Progressive Field. Meanwhile, the White Sox are working through things after they completed a sweep of the Astros in the best-of-three AL Wild Card Series on Wednesday to advance.
Chicago’s plan, understandably, is less settled coming off its Wild Card series, though Cleveland has some uncertainty as well. What could the pitching matchups look like? Let’s take a look.
Guardians
Messick has come a long way in one year. The lefty wasn’t on the Guardians’ roster in the 2025 AL Wild Card Series, following his seven-start debut stint in the Majors down the stretch. This spring, he had to earn a spot on Cleveland’s Opening Day roster. Now, the Guards are hoping he paves the way as they push for October glory.
Messick’s stellar rookie season could make him a finalist for both the AL Cy Young Award and the Rookie of the Year Award. The 25-year-old had a 2.56 ERA (seventh in MLB) in 186 1/3 innings over 32 starts, with 193 strikeouts and 49 walks. In perhaps a good omen, he was particularly effective against Chicago, logging a 2.81 ERA with 29 strikeouts and five walks in 25 2/3 innings over four starts.
If you like pitchers with overpowering stuff, Game 2 could be appointment viewing. This season, Williams racked up 248 strikeouts (second in MLB to Jacob Misiorowski’s 252) in 184 1/3 innings over 32 starts, all of which were career highs. He had double-digit punchouts in 11 of those outings, which led the Majors.
None of those 11 starts were against Chicago, though Williams did record a 3.98 ERA with 28 strikeouts and eight walks in 20 1/3 innings over four starts against the White Sox. His Game 2 assignment is noteworthy because it lines him up to pitch Game 5 (if necessary) back in Cleveland, whereas Messick is lined up for Game 4 in Chicago. Williams had a 2.84 ERA in 18 home starts this season, and a 5.05 ERA in 14 road starts.
The Guardians are still working through their plan here. Manager Stephen Vogt noted Thursday that they want to see how Games 1 and 2 go and what their potential needs are before making a decision.
Why could it be Espino? Of the 14 position players on the White Sox Wild Card Series roster, there were six lefties and one switch-hitter. Starting Espino as an opener for lefty Joey Cantillo could force Chicago to make a lineup decision, such as whether to start lefty smasher Randal Grichuk against Espino, or call his number after Cantillo enters.
Espino served as an opener in Cantillo’s final three appearances of the regular season after the lefty encountered some command issues. Cantillo tossed 15 scoreless innings, allowing five hits and four walks, while striking out 17 batters in those outings. The formula could work in October.
All that being said: The Guardians have a flurry of options, between Espino/Cantillo, Tanner Bibee and Foster Griffin. Stay tuned.
White Sox
Some of the TBDs in terms of White Sox starters were cleared up on Friday by manager Will Venable. It begins with Smith, the rookie southpaw, who gets the same Game 1 honor as he did in the sweep of Houston during the AL Wild Card Series.
“They're a really good team. This will be my third time playing [them] since I got up here,” Smith said Friday. “So just kind of familiar with the guys and their lineup and familiar with the scouting reports against them. We are both good teams. We play hard. They play hard. So it's going to be a good series.“
With Sunday’s off-day, Burke would be pitching on regular rest Monday after striking out eight over four innings against the Astros on Wednesday. Venable confirmed Friday that Burke will pitch on Monday and will not pitch on Saturday, but the skipper did not confirm if it would be as a starter or bulk hurler.
Burke recently joked that the White Sox have 13 pitchers, or 12 in the Wild Card round, but they don’t look at anyone as a starter or reliever. This is not a situation of trying to outsmart the opposition by usage of an opener, but it’s more about Venable and his staff trying to win each game and nothing more. It has produced one of the best Major League Baseball stories this season, so why change now?
Again, Kay would make sense, having last pitched Wednesday. But he might be needed in one of the first two games. Everything is fluid.
One thing to consider: Davis Martin has a 5-3 record with a 3.13 ERA over 15 home starts against a 4-5 record and 4.68 ERA over 14 appearances (13 starts) on the road. Let’s not forget rookie Noah Schultz, who has been impressive working multiple innings out of the bullpen, or rookie David Sandlin, a starter who worked in relief against the Astros. Sean Newcomb has done a little bit of everything this season, with a 3.24 ERA over eight games against the Guardians. So he’s always a possibility.
Don’t overlook Smith coming back, with Venable discussing Smith and Taylor potentially being available for all three games.

item.content:encoded:
Published Oct 2, 2026 10:17 am
NEW YORK (AP) — Chicago Cubs center fielder Pete Crow-Armstrong won the Baseball Digest major league player of the year award Friday, and Milwaukee Brewers ace Jacob Misiorowski was selected pitcher of the year.
San Diego Padres closer Mason Miller was chosen reliever of the year.
Crow-Armstrong batted .280 with 45 home runs and 41 stolen bases this season, becoming the seventh member of the 40-40 club.
He led the majors in runs (119), tied for most homers, ranked second in OPS (.943) and finished fourth in RBIs (107). All while playing outstanding defense and appearing in all 162 regular-season games to help the Cubs earn a National League wild card.
The 24-year-old Crow-Armstrong received 21 of 24 first-place votes in balloting by a panel of baseball writers, broadcasters, reporters and researchers that included several former players, managers and executives.
Houston Astros slugger Yordan Alvarez finished second.
Crow-Armstrong became the seventh Cubs player to win the Baseball Digest award and first since Kris Bryant and Anthony Rizzo shared the prize in 2016.
The hard-throwing Misiorowski also garnered 21 first-place votes after going 16-5 to propel Milwaukee to the best record in the big leagues (103-59) and its fourth consecutive NL Central title. He led the majors with a 1.80 ERA and 252 strikeouts in 30 starts covering 174 2/3 innings.
New York Yankees right-hander Cam Schlittler was runner-up to the 24-year-old Misiorowski, the first Brewers pitcher to take home the honor.
Miller, 28, tied for the NL lead with a career-high 38 saves as the Padres earned a wild-card spot in the playoffs. He went 5-2 with a 1.67 ERA and 129 strikeouts in 70 innings over 66 appearances.
The right-hander received 18 first-place votes and easily outpaced Cleveland Guardians closer Cade Smith, who came in second.

Milwaukee will take the field on Saturday night against the San Diego Padres at American Family Field in Game 1 of the National League Division Series. item.content:encoded:
After a few long days of waiting, we're finally just one day away from the Milwaukee Brewers kicking off their 2026 playoff run.
Milwaukee will take the field on Saturday night against the San Diego Padres at American Family Field in Game 1 of the National League Division Series. It's been a long road to get here, but the playoffs have arrived and unsurprisingly, the first pitch of the postseason for Milwaukee will be from Jacob Misiorowski.
The righty flamethrower was the best pitcher in baseball throughout the 2026 season and he will have a chance to give Milwaukee an early lead in the series. The Padres aren't an easy matchup, to say the least. Fortunately, Misiorowski has already had some success against San Diego this season.
Misiorowski made a start against the Padres back on May 13. That day, the big righty tossed seven shutout innings and allowed just four base hits while striking out 10 batters. While that stat line is a bit absurd, it's pretty much in line with what he did all season to this point.
Jacob Misiorowski Give Milwaukee An Advantage
Misiorowski was the best pitcher in the league. There's no denying that fact. He finished the regular season with a league-leading 1.80 ERA to go along with 252 strikeouts in 174 2/3 innings pitched. The most earned runs he allowed in a game was five on Sep. 2. That was the only game in which he allowed more than three runs in a game all season. Simply put, he gave Milwaukee a chance to win every single time he touched the mound.
So, when it comes to Game 1, that's the guy you want to roll with. He was the best pitcher in baseball all season in general, plus he had individual success against the Padres. What else could you ask for?
Last season, the big flamethrower made three postseason appearances and had a 1.50 ERA in 12 innings of work. That was after struggling down the stretch and having his role shifted a bit with the organization. In the offseason, he went back to the lab and made a leap ahead of the 2026 season. If he pitches as he has all season to this point, Milwaukee should be able to come out on top in the first game of the five-game series. That's critical. Whoever wins Game 1 has a significant advantage the rest of the way in the series.
Patrick McAvoy's experiences include local and national sports coverage at the New England Sports Network with a focus on baseball and basketball. Outside of journalism, Patrick received an MBA at Brandeis University. For all business/marketing inquiries regarding "Milwaukee Brewers On SI," please reach out to Scott Neville: scott@moreviewsmedia.com

item.title: [FanSided] MLB Power Rankings: Every remaining playoff team after Wild Card Round
item.dc:creator: Christopher Kline
item.description: With the exception of Braves-Phillies (of course), this year's Wild Card round was pretty lopsided. The competition should heat up in the Divisional Series, however. Not only are the best teams in each league being reintroduced, but we have division rivals and compelling stylistic contrasts. The Brewers and Padres could not be more different in how their teams were built. The Rays and Yankees don't like each other. The Guardians and White Sox also don't like each other. item.content:encoded:
With the exception of Braves-Phillies (of course), this year's Wild Card round was pretty lopsided. The competition should heat up in the Divisional Series, however. Not only are the best teams in each league being reintroduced, but we have division rivals and compelling stylistic contrasts.
The Brewers and Padres could not be more different in how their teams were built. The Rays and Yankees don't like each other. The Guardians and White Sox also don't like each other. As for Braves-Dodgers? Well, there's plenty of recent history there. But which teams have the look of title contenders as we move deeper into October? Let's rank all eight remaining teams in terms of championship equity.
8. Chicago White Sox
The White Sox made it hard on themselves down the stretch, but Chicago is riding high after a first-round sweep of the Astros, with blessings from the Pope. Coming into the postseason, the White Sox were broadly dinged for their youth and inexperience. As fate would have it, though, the South Siders were significantly more poised than a seasoned Astros team.
Chicago's lineup performed top to bottom. They worked deep into counts and made smart, situational swings. The rotation is still a mess, and the bullpen is not much better, but there's a lovable underdog quality to this White Sox team that is hard to ignore. By default, the White Sox rank last here, but an ALDS matchup with the Guardians is perfectly winnable. Do not discount the possibility of a South Siders pennant run.
7. Cleveland Guardians
Cleveland has been there and done that. This team is always the AL Central champ, it feels like, even when the odds are stacked against them. The Guardians hit much better down the stretch after a brutal start to the campaign, while their pitching is a potential superpower. Parker Messick and Gavin Williams can match just about any aces blow-for-blow, and this bullpen always tends to perform.
The question now becomes: Can Stephen Vogt's squad translate their signature Guards Ball style to October? The answer for years now has been "no." Cleveland lacks thump in the heart of the order, but tends to execute the small things — bunts, base-running, two-strike hitting — better than anyone. Chicago's pitching staff is vulnerable and the Guardians have the edge in experience, but so did Houston. And the Astros' bats were much better. The outcome of this series will not shock me in either direction, to be frank.
6. Atlanta Braves
The Braves lineup struggled down the stretch but appeared to wake up against the Phillies, especially in the clincher. Atlanta has no shortage of offensive talent and a deep bullpen, with plenty of postseason experience to draw on. So why ranked so low?
Well, the rotation is a mess. Chris Sale is an elite 1A, but Tyler Mahle is questionable against better offensive teams (see: Dodgers) and their third starter is Grant Holmes behind an opener. Atlanta has seven starters on the IL and could struggle to build a bridge to the stellar back end of their bullpen in non-Sale starts. That said, if the Braves' bats heat up, perhaps it does not matter. There is a clear break in quality between Cleveland at No. 7 and the rest of the field. The Braves are very, very capable of mounting a deep run. Atlanta notably went 5-1 against the Dodgers this season.
5. Tampa Bay Rays
The Rays just kept winning all season long. There was no more consistent force in the American League. We can quibble with the back half of their lineup and question the depth of their rotation, but the Rays are an extremely disciplined club with star power (Junior Caminero) and fundamental skills (Chandler Simpson, Jonny DeLuca) in equal measure.
Tampa is going to defend at a high level and run the bases with intent. Their pitching staff does not look so fearsome on paper, but Drew Rasmussen is a bonafide ace and Freddy Peralta looked more like himself in September. Whether this team can match the raw explosiveness of the Yankees' lineup is the swing factor. On the flip side, New York has a propensity for unforced errors that Tampa can ruthlessly capitalize on.
4. New York Yankees
The Yankees are still waiting on Aaron Judge. New York stuffed its Wild Card roster with platoon bats and situational hitters, but Aaron Boone probably needs more pitchers for a five-game Divisional Series. The lineup exploded against the Red Sox, but Tampa will almost certainly manage its pitching staff better than Chad Tracy and Boston did.
New York is the best team in the American League on paper, even with all their injuries, but the bullpen is perilously thin and it's hard to trust this lineup completely. Ben Rice has caught fire at an optimal moment, so there's that. And the Yankees boast, by far, the most star power of any team west of Los Angeles. Whether it can all come together against a healthy, well-rested Rays team remains to be seen.
3. Milwaukee Brewers
The Brewers, almost without fail, dominate the regular season despite ownership's pervasive cheapness. This team knows how to develop talent in-house and locate value on the margins. There is no better-run small-market clubhouse in MLB. And yet, Milwaukee has consistently fallen flat in the playoffs. Whether or not this year is any different comes down to a couple factors.
First, Jacob Misiorowski helps. Milwaukee has the best pitcher in baseball and he may damn near guarantee a Game 1 win in the NLDS. The Brewers' bullpen is rock solid, too, while the depth of their rotation is respectable. Milwaukee's pitching can win ballgames. More importantly, there's less elite competition than usual; even the Dodgers are scuttling at the plate, while the entire American League is poked full of holes. The path has never been clearer for the Brewers, who compensate for limited slug with impressive plate discipline and savvy situational hitting. If Milwaukee can maintain its extraordinarily high baseline, there's reason to believe this could be the year it all clicks.
2. San Diego Padres
There are few stars I trust more in a high-leverage spot than Fernando Tatis Jr. The man just makes good things happen, whether he's using his power or his speed. San Diego's entire lineup, really, has come on strong in the final month. After sputtering for much of the regular season, the likes of Jackson Merrill and Manny Machado have apparently remembered how talented they are. Gavin Sheets and Ty France are improbably major contributors. On the pitching front, Michael King and Nick Pivetta tore through a loaded Cubs lineup. The Padres' bullpen is the best in baseball, so no team can more easily build a bridge between their frontline starters and the ninth inning.
San Diego's rotation depth is suspect; once Walker Buehler and Robbie Ray are asked to carry several innings, it could get dicey. But in terms of momentum and top shelf star power, the Padres clear the majority of the competition around them. It can't hurt that San Diego plays the Dodgers as well as any team, either. That matchup could ultimately define the 2026 season, assuming the Padres can out-slug the No. 1 seed Brewers.
1. Los Angeles Dodgers
This shouldn't come as a shock. The Dodgers aren't as untouchable as their reputation suggests, but there's still only one team with Tarik Skubal, Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Blake Snell and Tyler Glasnow lined up on the mound. Meanwhile, Shohei Ohtani has proven his capacity for clutch swings time after time since arriving in Hollywood two years ago. Los Angeles has the best pitchers and the best player in MLB, with a star-studded lineup to boot. Mookie Betts, Kyle Tucker and Freddie Freeman weren't at the peak of their powers this season, but that's still a group worth trusting when every at-bat is magnified.
Los Angeles has depth, too. Josue De Paula is one of the most exciting young bats in baseball and the Dodgers barely have room for him on the roster. Alex Call and Dalton Rushing are useful as situational hitters. The primary concern is L.A.'s bullpen, but Rōki Sasaki, Kris Bubic and Justin Wrobleski — their excess rotation arms — should help the Dodgers cover innings when needed. The Dodgers are banged-up and very much vulnerable, but this is still the team to beat, full stop.
